headline: AI platforms and trusted components dominate the day's threat picture
standfirst: The day's security picture has three threads: confirmed exploitation is landing on AI infrastructure, cloud credentials remain a persistent route into corporate accounts, and researchers keep finding ways to abuse trusted components, from boot-time drivers to npm packages.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

The most urgent item is [[s22]], where CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog now covers three actively exploited flaws. Ray, the AI compute engine, has a critical pre-2.52.0 remote-code-execution hole reachable through a malicious website or malvertising. Its browser-attack guard is a User-Agent check that can be spoofed and combined with DNS rebinding, turning a developer who simply visits a page into a compromised build environment. MLflow, before 3.15.0, has an unauthenticated server-side request forgery: a webhook test endpoint validates the original URL but then follows redirects and re-resolves the hostname, opening a path to internal services and cloud metadata. Zimbra Collaboration Suite before 10.1.20 carries an OS command injection exploitable when the optional zimbra-snmp package is installed and SNMP notifications are enabled. The Zimbra entry needs more preconditions, but its KEV listing means attackers are already using it. For anyone running these components, the correct response is to treat them as actively targeted and patch.

## Breaches

Repeated victimization is the theme in [[s13]]. Toronto's Hospital for Sick Children disclosed another data theft, tied to a third-party application and involving employee data, after already absorbing a ransomware attack that disabled systems years ago. Attackers returning to a pediatric institution show that healthcare remains a favored target for its sensitive data and operational fragility.

Cloud credential hygiene is the blunt lesson in [[s9]]. More than 9,300 Amazon Web Services access keys exposed over about four years are still active and valid. That means full control over corporate accounts is sitting in logs, public repositories, or paste sites long after it should have been rotated. The problem is not the initial leak as much as the absence of detection and rotation.

[[s19]] confirms a different kind of breach: Russian network monitoring vendor Microolap acknowledged an intrusion after pro-Ukraine group Black Spark claimed a month-long presence in its network and reached internal systems including the EtherSensor platform. A vendor whose product is network visibility losing control of its own network is both a reputation hit and a reminder that claims of long dwell time should be treated as credible until proven otherwise.

## Research

[[s10]] shows that Microsoft Defender's own signed Boot Time Removal Tool driver can be abused to perform arbitrary kernel-level file and registry operations on Windows 7 through 11 25H2. Because the driver is legitimately signed and already on disk, attackers do not need to import an external driver or exploit a software flaw. The practical risk is that security products can be deleted before the OS fully boots, leaving the system effectively blind. Defenders need boot-time visibility and should stop treating signed Microsoft binaries as automatically safe.

The npm supply chain continues to deliver working backdoors. [[s4]] reports 14 trojanized packages posing as calendar and streak utilities that drop RedC2 4.0, a Linux backdoor with AI-assisted command-and-control. As soon as the module loads, it finds a bundled binary, marks it executable, and launches it as a detached background process. A developer who installs a harmless-looking utility ends up with a persistent implant on a machine likely connected to source code and deployment pipelines.

AI guardrails have a blind spot, as [[s15]] demonstrates. The "Cryptographic Context Injection" technique hides malicious instructions inside encrypted contexts and only decrypts them inside a trusted execution environment, so safety filters see only ciphertext. The technique bypasses guardrails in Grok and Gemini. The lesson is that prompt filtering cannot rely on inspecting input text that is opaque by design.

## Industry

The day's most constructive item is [[s6]]. OWASP's new AI top-10 list and Universal Skill Format give security teams a common language for AI add-on and agentic-skill risk, replacing ad hoc assessments with a structured blueprint. A standard skill format is a small but useful step toward making AI security review repeatable, just as traditional top-10 lists made web application risk easier to communicate.

selected.title: CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog
selected.excerpt: CISA has added one new vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation. CVE-2025-62593 Ray-Project Ray Code Injection Vulnerability This type of vulnerability is a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and poses significant risks to the federal enterprise. Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security…

kev.shortDescription: Ray-Project Ray contains a code injection vulnerability that could allow remote code execution. Developers using Ray as a development tool may be exposed to this vulnerability exploitable through Firefox and Safari.
kev.requiredAction: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.

nvd.description: Ray is an AI compute engine. Prior to version 2.52.0, developers working with Ray as a development tool can be exploited via a critical RCE vulnerability exploitable via Firefox and Safari. This vulnerability is due to an insufficient guard against browser-based attacks, as the current defense uses the User-Agent header starting with the string "Mozilla" as a defense mechanism. This defense is insufficient as the fetch specification allows the User-Agent header to be modified. Combined with a DNS rebinding attack against the browser, and this vulnerability is exploitable against a developer running Ray who inadvertently visits a malicious website, or is served a malicious advertisement (malvertising). This issue has been patched in version 2.52.0.

kev.shortDescription: MLflow contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that can allow attackers to reach internal or cloud metadata services and receive response_status and response_body.
kev.requiredAction: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.

nvd.description: MLflow is an open source AI engineering platform for agents, large language models, and machine learning models. Prior to 3.15.0, the unauthenticated POST /api/2.0/mlflow/webhooks/{id}/test endpoint calls _validate_webhook_url() in mlflow/utils/validation.py only for the original URL while mlflow/webhooks/delivery.py follows redirects and re-resolves the hostname without pinning the validated address, allowing attackers to reach internal or cloud metadata services and receive response_status and response_body. This issue is fixed in version 3.15.0.

kev.vulnerabilityName: Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) OS Command Injection Vulnerability
kev.shortDescription: Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) contains an OS command injection vulnerability which could allow an unauthenticated attacker to send specially crafted SMTP requests that may result in execution of arbitrary operating system commands as the Zimbra user.
kev.requiredAction: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.

nvd.description: A remote code execution vulnerability exists in Zimbra Collaboration (ZCS) before 10.1.20 when the optional zimbra-snmp package is installed and SNMP notifications are enabled. Due to improper sanitization of untrusted input during SNMP notification processing, an unauthenticated attacker can send specially crafted SMTP requests that may result in execution of arbitrary operating system commands as the Zimbra user.

selected.angle: CISA KEV adds Ray, MLflow, and Zimbra flaws—active exploitation of critical RCEs in AI and mail platforms; Ray alone can hit developers via a malicious website.
